assign.request: 336px-tall .tabs.block .tab-bar on /framework/ext/catalog/ at 390 (341 at 720, normal 57 at 1280) — a blank grey band no LayoutTool rule catches. Also: page title spills 88px/23% past its container at 390 on the same page. Reproduce, decide what a tab bar should do on a phone, fix at the right rung, verify across other Doc pages, describe the rule gap. Dispatched by mastermind-layout.
steps: Decide what a tab bar should do on a phone
Fix at the right rung, in fence
Verify the title escape is covered
Verify across a sample of Doc pages + real catalog() callers, 4 widths
Describe the LayoutTool rule gap (no code)

assign.now: reproducing at 390/720/1280 with headless Playwright (global install, not the driven MCP tabs)

log.msg: Reproduced: .tab-bar is NOT wrapping into multiple rows anywhere -- it stays flex-wrap:nowrap, one row, four short tabs (Overview/API/Docs/Files) at every width. The 336px (390) / 341px (720) box height is the CONTAINER, with the single 39px row of tabs pinned to its BOTTOM edge (align-items:flex-end) -- a huge blank band above them, not wrapped rows. Correction to the dispatch's working theory.

assign.now: tracing root cause: why does .tab-bar's own box inflate to 336px

log.msg: ROOT CAUSE FOUND: a class-name collision, not a tabs bug. Doc.render() stamps every Doc page with `.ac("page-" + this.name)` (Page.css convention) -- and this page's own route segment IS "catalog", so the outer .page.doc-page ends up wearing the class `page-catalog`. catalog.css's mobile media query (@media max-width:64em) has `.page-catalog { flex-direction: column; }` with NO guard -- unlike the base-layer rule right above it (`.page-catalog:where(:not(.page))`, catalog.css:15) which was written with exactly this collision in mind, in a comment, back when the module was built. The unguarded mobile rule flips .page.doc-page's own flex-direction to column below 1024px. doc.css's `.tab-bar { flex: 1 1 24em; }` (a WIDTH basis, written assuming row layout) then gets reinterpreted as a HEIGHT basis once the axis flips: 24em x the mobile font-size (~14px) = 336px measured (390: 14x24=336 exact; 720: 14.2x24=340.8, measured 341; 1280 is >64em so the collision rule never fires there, row stays, height a normal 57px). The 88px/23% title escape on the same page is the SAME bug: in the corrupted column layout, .doc-well (holding the h1) also lost its row-mode width constraint and measured 478px inside a 390px box.

assign.now: deciding what a tab bar should do on a phone

log.msg: DECISION: no redesign needed -- the existing design is already correct and was never actually reached. tabs.css already says (comment, .tab-bar rule): "One strip that scrolls, never a wrapping block" -- flex-wrap:nowrap + overflow:auto, i.e. horizontal-scroll, chosen over wrap-and-accept-height, collapse-to-select, or shrink-the-tabs. doc.css layers a second, compatible decision on top for the title+bar ROW specifically: when the bar's 24em flex-basis doesn't fit beside the title, the WHOLE BAR (not individual tabs) wraps to its own line below the title, landing the tab labels on the title's left axis. Both decisions were sound and already implemented; the defect was a paint-time collision preventing them from rendering, not a design gap. No tradeoff to record beyond what's already documented in tabs.css/doc.css.

assign.now: fixing at the right rung: catalog.css, adding the guard the base rule already has

log.msg: FIX: catalog.css:145, `.page-catalog { flex-direction: column; }` -> `.page-catalog:where(:not(.page)) { flex-direction: column; }` inside the existing @media(max-width:64em) block -- the identical guard the unaffected base-layer rule already carries (catalog.css:15), for the identical collision. One line, in fence. Verified with headless Playwright at 390/720/1280 (real dev server, port 80, not the MCP-driven tabs): tab-bar height 336->39 (390), 341->54 (720, now correctly sharing the title's row since it fits), 57 unchanged (1280). doc-well width 478->153 at 390 -- the 88px/23% title escape is fixed by the SAME one-line change, since it was the same root cause. No separate title fix needed.

assign.now: verifying across other Doc pages and real catalog() callers, 4 widths

log.msg: Verified no regression. Other Doc pages (core/App, core/View) were never affected -- their route segments aren't literally "catalog", so the collision never applied; confirmed still 39px @390 / 57px @1280 after the fix, byte-identical to before. Real catalog() callers (framework/ui/, framework/styles/sections/) still get the intended mobile behaviour post-fix: flex-direction:column, previews strip scrolling horizontally at 390 (e.g. sections/: 390x160 strip), row+sticky rail at 1280 (286x1000) -- the guard only ever excluded the coincidentally-.page-classed Doc wrapper, never the real .page-catalog div (which has no .page class). Screenshots (mcp__site__shot) at 390/720/1280/3440 on /framework/ext/catalog/ confirm: 390 now shows the bar wrapped correctly below the title at its true ~40px height; 720 now fits title+bar on one row (title 155px + bar 340px basis < 720, no wrap needed); 1280/3440 unchanged (57px, already outside the 64em collision window).

RULE GAP (finding only, not added -- out of fence): the 88px title escape WAS already caught by LayoutTool's existing `escape` rule (that's how the mobile sweep found it). The 336px band was caught by NOTHING. The shape that slipped through: a flex/grid container whose own rendered height is a large multiple of its children's collective content height, with the children pinned to one edge (align-items: flex-end/flex-start, not centered/stretched) rather than filling it -- i.e. a big BLANK REGION inside one element's own box, not an overflow past a parent and not a full-viewport dead zone. `dead-space` doesn't apply (needs 4+ text blocks over 20 chars, and reads the viewport, not one element). `escape` doesn't apply (nothing overflows a parent -- the box IS the blank space; its bounds are entirely self-consistent). A rule comparing a container's own height against the union bounding box of its immediate children, flagging e.g. height > ~3x that union with the children edge-anchored rather than distributed, would have caught this one directly. Left for Mike to weigh -- it's a narrower, rarer shape than the existing rules and may not be worth a general rule for one collision bug, but it is a real blind spot: the exact failure the dispatch prompt asked after ("a large blank grey band... no rule currently watches for this") produces no finding at any severity, at any width, today.

assign.outcome: **Fixed: the 336px tab-bar band was a class-name collision, not a tabs design flaw.** `/framework/ext/catalog/`'s own Doc page happens to have route segment "catalog", so Page.render()'s `page-<name>` stamp gave it the class `page-catalog` -- colliding with the REAL `.page-catalog` class this module's own rail/strip layout owns. catalog.css's mobile media query flipped that collided element's flex-direction to column, turning doc.css's `.tab-bar { flex: 1 1 24em }` (a width basis) into a height basis: 24em x mobile font-size = 336px (390) / 341px (720), with the tab row pinned to its bottom edge -- never wrapped rows, contrary to the dispatch's working theory. The 88px/23% title escape on the same page was the identical bug (the title's box lost its row-mode width constraint too). One-line fix in fence, catalog.css:145 -- added the SAME `:where(:not(.page))` guard the unaffected base-layer rule (catalog.css:15) already carries for this exact collision. Both bugs gone with one change; verified at 390/720/1280/3440 on /framework/ext/catalog/, plus no regression on core/App and core/View (Doc pages never affected) and no regression on real catalog() callers (framework/ui/, framework/styles/sections/ -- mobile strip / desktop rail both intact). No redesign: tabs.css's existing decision (horizontal-scroll strip, never wrap individual tabs) and doc.css's existing decision (wrap the WHOLE bar below the title when it doesn't fit) were both already correct, just never reached. LayoutTool rule gap described in the log (not added, out of fence): no rule compares a container's own height against its children's collective content height with children edge-anchored -- the shape that let a self-consistent 336px blank box (nothing overflowing, nothing off-viewport) pass every existing check.
